goal: Overall task (run 12, goal a): on this Linux machine, get QEMU set up with OP-TEE, i.e. build OP-TEE for QEMU Armv8-A (qemu_v8) from the official OP-TEE manifest and build repositories, and later boot it in QEMU. Work in the current directory; the OP-TEE source tree must live in ./optee (the repo client root). You may use sudo -n if it is available. The work is split into sub-goals; this one is: boot the built qemu_v8 setup in QEMU non-interactively (no terminal windows or GUI) and show that OP-TEE starts in the secure world, Linux boots to a login prompt, and OP-TEE is usable from Linux (for example with xtest). Leave the normal-world console log in optee/out/bin/serial0.log and the secure-world log in optee/out/bin/serial1.log. Do not rebuild unless the boot needs it.

checks.cmd: cd optee/build && test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)" && git fetch -q "${OPTEE_BUILD_UPSTREAM:-https://github.com/OP-TEE/build.git}" master && git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD FETCH_HEAD && head -c 4 ../qemu/build/qemu-system-aarch64 | grep -q ELF && { command -v expect >/dev/null || sudo -n apt-get install -y -q expect >/dev/null; } && rm -f ../out/bin/serial0.log ../out/bin/serial1.log && PATH=$HOME/bin:$PATH timeout 1500 make check-only CHECK_TESTS=xtest XTEST_ARGS=1001 TIMEOUT=300
